body.html:
In a disturbing incident from Amehra village under the Ganganagar police station area of Meerut, a 45-year-old man named Famid died under suspicious circumstances at the Naya Savera De-Addiction Center.

articles.title: Man Seen Washing ‘Disposable’ Food Trays Inside Amrit Bharat Express Coach
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking video from the Erode–Jogbani Amrit Bharat Express (Train No. 16601) has gone viral, showing a man allegedly washing used disposable meal trays inside the passenger compartment, raising major concerns over hygiene and food safety on Indian Railways.

body.html:
A shocking video from the Erode–Jogbani Amrit Bharat Express (Train No. 16601) has gone viral, showing a man allegedly washing used disposable meal trays inside the passenger compartment, raising major concerns over hygiene and food safety on Indian Railways.

The incident reportedly occurred during one of the train’s recent journeys. The video, filmed by a passenger, shows a man — believed to be part of the railway catering staff — cleaning and stacking plastic meal trays at a washbasin meant for passengers. When questioned, he nervously claimed the containers were being “sent back,” but couldn’t explain why they were being washed in the passenger area instead of the pantry car.

The video has since gone viral, with social media users tagging @RailMinIndia and @IRCTCofficial, demanding an inquiry. One post alleged, “A scam worth crores — passengers are being served dirty, reused containers washed with filthy water.”

In response, Indian Railways clarified that “the casseroles were used only once, not reused for serving food. They were being cleaned before disposal, as verified through a factual investigation. Please don’t spread misleading information.”

The Erode–Jogbani Amrit Bharat Express runs once a week, covering over 3,100 km across multiple states from Tamil Nadu to Bihar. Experts warn that reusing disposable containers can pose severe health hazards, especially when serving hot meals, as plastic can release toxic chemicals.

articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic incident from Lucknow’s Indira Nagar area has left residents stunned after a 13-year-old boy died under mysterious circumstances while reportedly playing the popular mobile game Free Fire.

body.html:
A tragic incident from Lucknow’s Indira Nagar area has left residents stunned after a 13-year-old boy died under mysterious circumstances while reportedly playing the popular mobile game Free Fire.

The deceased, identified as Vivek (13), originally from Sitapur, had recently moved with his family to Parmeshwar Enclave Colony just eight days ago. According to relatives, Vivek was deeply addicted to mobile gaming and had been playing Free Fire alone at home on Wednesday.

His sister Anju said she had stepped out for a short while, and upon returning, found Vivek lying unconscious with his phone still in hand. Initially assuming he had fallen asleep, she soon realized something was wrong when he didn’t respond. The family rushed him to Lohia Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Police from Indira Nagar station reached the spot and have taken the body for post-mortem. Officials stated that the exact cause of death is yet to be determined, and a thorough investigation is underway.

articles.title: Mid-Air Panic: Air China Flight Makes Emergency Landing After Battery Fire Erupts in Cabin
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Shanghai: A major scare unfolded aboard Air China flight CA139 from Hangzhou to Seoul on Saturday when a lithium battery in a passenger’s cabin bag caught fire mid-air, forcing the aircraft to make an emergency landing at Shanghai Pudong International Airport.

body.html:
Shanghai: A major scare unfolded aboard Air China flight CA139 from Hangzhou to Seoul on Saturday when a lithium battery in a passenger’s cabin bag caught fire mid-air, forcing the aircraft to make an emergency landing at Shanghai Pudong International Airport.

According to the airline, the fire broke out shortly after takeoff, originating from a battery kept in an overhead luggage compartment.
Videos circulating on social media show panic-stricken passengers screaming as thick smoke fills the cabin, while flight attendants rush with fire extinguishers to contain the blaze. The passengers can be heard shouting “Hurry up!” as the crew battles the flames.

Air China confirmed that the crew acted swiftly, extinguishing the fire within minutes and diverting the flight to Shanghai as a precaution. The aircraft landed safely, and no injuries were reported.

The flight, which had departed Hangzhou at 9:47 a.m., was originally scheduled to arrive at Incheon International Airport at 12:20 p.m. local time. Following the emergency landing, passengers were provided assistance and rebooked to continue their journey.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the battery fire, with aviation experts once again highlighting the dangers of carrying lithium batteries in unchecked or poorly packed conditions.

articles.title: Massive Fire Erupts at Dhaka Airport Cargo Terminal, Flights Suspended Amid Emergency Response
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Dhaka (Bangladesh): A massive fire broke out on Saturday afternoon at the cargo terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, forcing authorities to suspend all flight operations temporarily as firefighting and rescue efforts continue.

body.html:
Dhaka (Bangladesh): A massive fire broke out on Saturday afternoon at the cargo terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, forcing authorities to suspend all flight operations temporarily as firefighting and rescue efforts continue.

The blaze began around 2:30 pm (local time) near Gate 8 of the Cargo Village, an area used for storing imported goods. Thick plumes of black smoke engulfed large parts of Dhaka, prompting a full-scale emergency response.

According to officials, over 30 firefighting units — including teams from the Fire Service, Civil Aviation Authority, Air Force, Navy, and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) — were deployed to control the inferno. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) confirmed that all major emergency agencies are jointly working to contain the fire.

Flight operations at Dhaka’s main airport have been fully suspended, and several inbound flights diverted to Chattogram’s Shah Amanat International Airport and Sylhet’s Osmani International Airport. Authorities clarified that no aircraft were damaged in the incident.

As of now, no casualties or major injuries have been reported. Officials said the cause of the fire is under investigation, and normal flight services will resume once the area is declared safe.
